brief.t: Set up in 2000 as a joint venture of HDFC Ltd and UK's Standard Life; listed on NSE and BSE in November 2017. Standard Life (now abrdn) sold its last shares in 2023.
Since HDFC Ltd merged into HDFC Bank on 1 July 2023, HDFC Bank is the parent (promoter). In June 2026 HDFC Bank put in another ₹1,000 crore of fresh capital.
Vibha Padalkar has been MD & CEO since 2018; in 2026 she was re-appointed for five more years from 12 Sep 2026 (IRDAI approved). Keki Mistry is Chairman.
FY 2025-26 profit was ₹1,910 crore (+6%), held back by the loss of GST input tax credit and new labour codes. In H1 FY27 (Apr–Sep 2026) profit was ₹1,119 crore (+13%).
Sells mostly through banks (about 58% of individual sales, led by HDFC Bank), plus agents, other partners and online. ULIPs are the biggest product (45% of individual APE in H1 FY27).

timeline.t: Incorporated as HDFC Standard Life, a joint venture of HDFC Ltd and Standard Life.
IPO at ₹290 a share; listed on NSE and BSE on 17 Nov 2017.
Vibha Padalkar became MD & CEO, succeeding Amitabh Chaudhry.
Exide Life Insurance (bought for ₹6,687 crore) merged into HDFC Life after IRDAI's final approval.
abrdn (ex-Standard Life) sold its last stake in May; HDFC Bank became the parent after the HDFC merger on 1 July.
₹1,000 crore capital from HDFC Bank (June); Padalkar's new five-year term began on 12 September.

model.how: HDFC Life collects premiums from people who buy life cover, savings, pension or annuity plans. It invests this money (₹4.1 lakh crore AUM) in bonds and shares, pays claims and maturity benefits, and keeps a profit from the gap between what it earns, what it promises customers and its costs. Most policies are sold through HDFC Bank and other bank partners.
flow: Customer buys a policy via a bank, agent, partner or online
Pays claims, maturities, annuities and surrenders
Profit = investment and risk margins minus commissions and costs

industry.regulator: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)
points: From 22 Sep 2025 GST was removed on individual life policies. Customers pay less, but insurers lost input tax credit, which squeezed margins in FY26.
In Sep 2026 IRDAI proposed lower commissions and lower expense limits for insurers. Insurance shares fell sharply; the rules are still at the consultation stage.
Big theme for interviews: growing protection (term) sales and holding margins while commission and cost rules get tighter.

frameworks.note: Framework views are analysis built from the verified facts on this page, not company statements.

glossary.Net profit: What is left after all costs and taxes. The company's final earnings.
glossary.Revenue: Total money earned from the business in a period, before costs.
glossary.Dividend: Part of the profit paid to shareholders, per share.
glossary.Attrition: The % of employees who leave in a year. Also called employee turnover.
glossary.IPO: Initial Public Offering: when a company first sells its shares to the public.
glossary.Market share: A company's sales as a % of the total sales of its industry.
glossary.Consolidated: Figures for the company together with its subsidiaries. 'Standalone' means the parent company alone.
glossary.BRSR: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report: an official yearly report on people, environment and governance that big listed companies must publish.
glossary.KYC: Know Your Customer: checking a customer's identity before opening an account or selling a product.
glossary.IRDAI: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India: the regulator of all insurance companies.
glossary.Premium: The money a customer pays to buy an insurance policy.
glossary.Gross written premium: Total premium collected in a period, from new and renewing policies.
glossary.New business premium: Premium from policies sold for the first time in the period.
glossary.Renewal premium: Premium paid by existing customers to keep their policies going.
glossary.APE: Annualised Premium Equivalent: a standard measure of new sales. Regular premiums count fully, single premiums count 10%.
glossary.VNB: Value of New Business: the expected future profit (today's value) from policies sold in the period. A key measure for life insurers.
glossary.VNB margin: VNB as a % of APE. Shows how profitable new sales are.
glossary.Embedded value: The value of a life insurer today: its net worth plus the present value of future profits from existing policies.
glossary.Persistency: The % of customers who keep paying premiums after a set time (e.g. 13th month, 61st month). Higher is better.
glossary.Solvency ratio: Available capital compared with the capital the regulator requires. IRDAI's minimum is 150% (1.5 times).
glossary.AUM: Assets Under Management: the money the insurer invests on behalf of policyholders and shareholders.
glossary.Protection: Pure risk cover such as term insurance: pays only if something happens, cheap premium, high profit margin.
glossary.ULIP: Unit Linked Insurance Plan: part insurance, part market investment. Returns depend on markets.
glossary.Par / Non-par: Participating (par) policies share profits through bonuses; non-participating (non-par) policies give fixed, guaranteed benefits.
glossary.Annuity: A product that pays a regular income, usually after retirement, in return for a lump sum.
glossary.Bancassurance: Selling insurance through a bank's branches and customers. A main channel for bank-backed insurers.
glossary.Agency: Selling insurance through individual commission-based agents.
glossary.Surrender: When a customer exits a policy early and gets back part of the money.
glossary.Claim settlement ratio: The % of claims an insurer pays out of those it receives. Higher means more claims paid.
glossary.GST on insurance: Tax charged on premiums. From 22 Sep 2025 the government removed GST on individual life and health policies.
glossary.Bima Sugam: An IRDAI online marketplace planned to let customers buy, compare and service insurance in one place.
glossary.Input tax credit: GST paid on a company's own costs (like commissions and rent) that it can normally deduct from GST it collects. With GST removed on life policies, insurers lost this credit.
glossary.Expense of management: An insurer's total costs (commissions plus operating expenses) as a % of premium. IRDAI sets a limit.
glossary.Preferential issue: Selling new shares directly to a chosen investor (here, the parent HDFC Bank) to raise capital.
glossary.Operating RoEV: Operating return on embedded value: how fast the insurer's embedded value grows from its core business in a year.

Role knowledge, the company and HR questions

Finance.q: What is VNB margin and what was HDFC Life's latest figure?
Finance.a: VNB is the value of future profits from policies sold in the period; VNB margin is VNB divided by APE. HDFC Life's was 24.7% in H1 FY27, up from 24.5%.

Finance.q: Why did HDFC Life's FY26 profit grow only 6%?
Finance.a: GST was removed on individual policies from Sep 2025, so it lost input tax credit, and new labour codes added costs. Excluding these, the company says profit grew 16%.

Finance.q: What is a solvency ratio and why did HDFC Bank invest ₹1,000 crore?
Finance.a: It compares available capital with what IRDAI requires (minimum 150%). It fell to 177% in Mar 2026, so the parent added capital; it was 180% in Sep 2026.

Marketing.q: How would you get more young people to buy term insurance?
Marketing.a: Explain it simply as cheap family protection, use digital journeys and bank apps, show the GST saving, and use stories, not jargon.

Marketing.q: HDFC Life sells most policies through banks. How can it grow other channels?
Marketing.a: Build its agency network in smaller towns, add new bank and NBFC partners (like the new J&K Bank tie-up) and grow online sales.

HR.q: How would you reduce early attrition among new insurance advisors?
HR.a: Better selection, strong first-90-day training and mentoring, quick first earnings, digital sales tools and recognition.

Sales.a: Ask about family and loans, show how a small yearly premium protects them, mention no GST on individual policies, and the company's claims track record.

Operations.a: Auto-debit mandates, renewal reminders in local languages, easy online payment, and early calls to customers likely to stop paying.

Other.q: What do IRDAI's 2026 commission proposals mean for HDFC Life?
Other.a: Lower commissions and expense caps could cut costs for customers but change bank and broker incentives; management expects agency to be least affected. The rules are still a consultation.

interview.why_us: HDFC Life has protected Indian families for over 25 years and, with HDFC Bank as its parent, reaches customers across the country. It is growing term protection fast, kept margins steady through the GST change, and is investing in technology and new partners. I want to learn insurance at a company that combines a trusted brand with strong financial discipline, and contribute to [your role].
ask: How is the company preparing for IRDAI's proposed commission and expense rules?
How will HDFC Life grow agency and other channels beyond HDFC Bank?
What does success look like for a new joiner in the first six months?

gd.for: Lower costs for customers and less mis-selling of high-commission products.
gd.against: Insurance is 'sold, not bought'; lower pay may reduce advisors and slow the spread of cover.

gd.t: Should banks sell insurance to their customers?
gd.for: Banks have trust and reach, so more people get insured quickly.
gd.against: Risk of mis-selling and pushing products along with loans.

avoid: Don't call it 'HDFC Standard Life' today; the name changed and Standard Life (abrdn) exited in 2023.
Don't mix H1 FY27 profit (₹1,119 cr) with Q2 FY27 profit (₹508 cr).
Don't say IRDAI's 2026 commission caps are final; they are still proposals.
